metricCaveats: Playwright durations cover the complete test, including login, interactions, accessibility checks and waits; they are not endpoint response times.

collectPerformance reads performance navigation[0], DOMContentLoaded event end and LCP. It does not retain the navigation entry URL, request waterfall or redirect timing, so the logged metric cannot by itself distinguish initial login navigation from a subsequent protected navigation.
The instructor case failed only after TTFB<=3000 passed, at DOMContentLoaded=11307; later load/LCP assertions were not reached on that first attempt.
Both runs had one quality budget failure recovered by the existing CI retry. Playwright labels this flaky, but that label is not a root-cause explanation.
independentObservations: The instructor group+session path was already exercised successfully by the mutation suite at 14:08:48Z-14:09:12Z, before the quality suite at 14:10:30Z; this is not evidence of a first-ever server render of that path.
The public login quality test stayed similar (3.9s vs3.7s); admin quality improved (10.3s vs8.0s). These do not support uniform slowdown of every request.

The two successful communication role tests were slower in the new run (parent7.0s->11.6s, admin9.6s->16.6s), while owner/instructor URL transitions exceeded their 5s assertion. This is consistent with delay affecting multiple protected flows during that step, but does not identify server, database, network or browser cause.

httpConsoleEvidence.reason: Quality suite does not collect response/console failure events. Communication collects them but asserts only after navigation/page checks; owner/instructor aborted before this assertion. No retained quality/communication artifact contains a request waterfall.

retainedArtifactLimitation: 35514772810 exposes only the exact-source and earlier seven-theme matrix artifacts. 35512095754 also retains Priority A and release evidence. Neither exposes the quality-performance JSONs or communication failure reports; theme upload preceded those suites.
conclusion: A real second-case quality budget miss and two real communication login transition timeouts occurred. Prior b551 also exceeded a different quality metric. Available evidence cannot establish cold rendering or general infrastructure latency as the cause; protected-navigation request timing and error observations are needed from the focused precheck.
